newsitem.title: FRANCE: Essilor to focus on cutting debt.
newsitem.headline: Essilor to focus on cutting debt.

text.p: French lens maker Essilor International will strive to cut its debt inflated by the acquisition of four U.S. laboratories, chairman Xavier Fontanet said on Tuesday.

"Our obsession is to lower our debt as quickly as possible. We are hoping to bring it to less than 40 percent (of equity) at end 1997 and go towards 30 percent as soon as possible," Fontanet told a news conference.
Last year Essilor bought four U.S. optics laboratories for a little over 1.5 billion francs.
Net debt stood at 1.770 billion francs at end 1996 against 710 million francs at end 1995.
The gearing ratio jumped to 43 percent at end 1996 against 20 percent at end 1995.

Director general Philippe Alfroid said the conversion of preferred non-voting shares into common shares and the exercise of convertible bonds would generate 428 million francs, allowing it to cut debt and raise equity.
The convertible bonds would bring in 225 million francs in equity and the shares exchange some 203 million francs.
Operating profit rose to 981 million francs in 1996 from 865 million francs in 1995. But operating profit accounted for 12.5 percent of turnover against 13.2 percent in 1995.
The decline resulted mostly from the acquisition of the four U.S. labs, whose operating profit to turnover ratio stood at only 5.3 percent.
Alfroid said that in 1997 the four U.S. labs may improve their profit to turnover ratio to between 6.5 and seven percent.
Chairman Xavier Fontanet said Essilor was aiming for an operating profitability of 13 to 14 percent on the long-term.
He also said Essilor was considering transferring production from some units to countries with lower production costs.
In the United States, the group plans to transfer production from some of its Florida plants to Mexico and Asia, he said.
"In 1997 and in following years we are expecting a sharp improvement in results in the United States," he said.
Essilor is also mulling acquisitions in Europe, Asia and India but Fontanet did not provide any details.
He also would not make an earnings forecast for 1997, saying, "We are extremely cautious"
He said 1997 started on a "sluggish" note, with a sharp slowdown in Germany weighing on European activities but that Asian operations were doing well.
